articles.title: Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility

While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership.

Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

articles.title: Fatal disagreement: on the COP31 summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Developed nations must bear much of the cost of carbon emissions

COP31 ended in Antalya, Türkiye, with a whimper. The 190-odd countries that had convened for nearly 12 days — a close to 50-hour overshoot — failed to agree on an overarching political statement , called a cover text, that acts as a stepping stone to future, collective global action on climate change. Usually, cover texts evolve as a final synthesis of deliberations ; the COP31 leadership, helmed by Türkiye and Australia, thought it fit to push for a cover text early in the proceedings. The headline sought was a global electrification target: 35% of global final energy consumption will come from electricity by 2035, in the hope that this would reduce direct fossil fuel emissions. Ultimately, the cover text failed to pass muster because the European Union objected to the text’s lack of any explicit mention of ‘fossil fuel,’ let alone its phase-out. The COP process is arduously protracted as even a single country’s objection can stall progress. Country-blocks outside the EU, such as coalitions of the least developed countries, island nations, some South American countries — reportedly 130 countries — were also insistent on fossil fuel language. While COP 31 made some progress on old pathways, such as the Just Transition agreement, it is perplexing that the delegations could not make progress on the other big prong of negotiations: climate finance.

The increase in solar panel installations and the significant shift towards battery use in grid storage and transport did not come cheap: the cost of the land required for their installation, their intermittent nature of being dependent on weather, grid upgrades all carry costs. It is global markets, imperfectly connected, but connected, that have managed to bring it to this stage over decades. India and China, major fossil emitters, with large, still indigent populations, are also leaders in total clean energy installations. Therefore it stands to reason that developed countries, which have committed to providing climate finance in recognition of their historical emissions, make good on past promises to shoulder the cost of the carbon emissions that are responsible for warming. Economic crises are a feature, and not a bug, of the interconnected financial system enveloping the world and there are, undeniably, challenges to diverting the necessary finance towards countries most vulnerable to climate change impact. However, it is no longer prudent to sweep this under the rug by scuttling experimental approaches — namely carbon capture — as inimical to the broader commitment to eschew fossil fuel. When the primary framework climate agreement was crafted three decades ago, nobody envisaged AI and the drain that data centres portended or the wars that would see the vociferous antagonists of coal immediately shore up their gas reserves. Without honest good-faith dialogue, the COP is at risk of being a sideshow: a mortal blow to multilateralism.

articles.title: Just verdict: on Myanmar and the International Court of Justice
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Rohingya cannot return unless Myanmar turns democratic

On November 19, the International Court of Justice held that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. It is for the first time that the court has found any state responsible for the crime. The verdict, with nine votes to six, was not lightly reached. Genocide requires proof of an intent to destroy a group. In the absence of direct evidence of a plan, the court could infer that intent only if it was “the only reasonable inference” from the facts, a high bar to affix responsibility. The facts it accepted are harrowing. In 2017, in what Myanmar’s army called “clearance operations” against the insurgent Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, 1,834 raped and 392 villages destroyed in northern Rakhine State. Over 7,00,000 fled to Bangladesh. Then Army chief Min Aung Hlaing, now Myanmar’s “civilian” President, called the “Bengali problem” an “unfinished job”. Myanmar argued that it had only been fighting insurgents or at worst, driving the Rohingya out or punishing them. The court said that the army drew no distinction between fighters and civilians, had no plan to move anyone, fired on fleeing people and killed children on a scale that could not be explained as punishment. Seen alongside decades of discrimination, the evidence pointed to an intent to destroy.

The incidents of 2017 were no aberration. The army drove lakhs of Rohingya into Bangladesh in 1978 and 1991-92. The junta stripped the Rohingya of citizenship in 1982 and the state branded them as “foreigners” in Arakan, disenfranchising them in 2015. While the junta’s Bamar-Buddhist vision has oppressed every minority, the Rohingya have been subjected to the most brutality. More than 1.2 million are in Bangladesh, living in dilapidated conditions, made worse due to diminished international aid. The court ordered Myanmar to allow their safe, voluntary and dignified return and to compensate them, but it has no means of enforcing its judgment. Only the UN Security Council can, but it will be subject to vetoes by Myanmar’s backers, China and Russia. On the very day of the verdict, the two joined the U.S. in Shenzhen to declare the “immunities of State officials” of “paramount importance”. Others, India among them, have courted the regime in Naypyitaw regardless, following sham elections that made the junta leader civilian President earlier this year. And Rakhine State, mired in civil war, is now mostly held by the Arakan Army which is accused of atrocities against the Rohingya. Only a truly democratic, federal, plural and peaceful Myanmar can bring the Rohingya home in safety.

articles.title: Core accountability: On core sector performance
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth

The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

Editorial Context: Core accountability: On core sector performance. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Climate action has to be timely, with adequate resources and monitoring

That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha.

Together with the CAMPA, NAP, and MGNREGS funds never materialising, it is no surprise that the programmes to improve forest quality and forest cover have respectively fallen short by 91.8% and 97.5% vis-à-vis the 2014 target. The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. Pro-climate work in practice ought to span government schemes to deliver action and justice, and the Ministry ought to have formalised the division of responsibilities and accounting system. The PAC’s new demand that the Ministry submit an implementation timetable is insufficient. From the Jal Shakti Abhiyan in 2019 to the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024, the government has often floated new programmes banking significantly on funds from existing schemes — an untenable policy when the latter also have their own obligations. And if the VB-G RAM G scheme was to also advance climate justice, the government should not have undermined the erstwhile demand-driven funding model and shifted more financial responsibility to the States. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are implemented.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Assam CM downplays ‘fight’ between two IPS officers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The confrontation occurred at an Assam Police battalion headquarters in the western part of the State on November 22, 2026
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) downplayed an alleged clash between two senior Indian Police Service officers at a party as a “personal fight”.

The incident, involving a Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) and a Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), occurred at an Assam Police battalion in the western part of the State on Sunday night (November 22, 2026).

“There was a fight between two persons at a private programme. We have nothing to do here, as it was personal and had no connection with the Police Department. Sometimes, we also end up having arguments,” the Chief Minister told journalists on the sidelines of an official event.
“We would have done something had it happened during official duty. I have no comment on a personal matter,” he said.
According to reports, the DIG in question was among several senior police officers invited to a party the SSP had organised.
The DIG and the SSP allegedly quarrelled during the event. It turned physical, reportedly leaving the SSP injured.
Another senior IPS officer, reportedly assigned by Director General of Police Harmeet Singh, resolved the matter.

Assam CM downplays ‘fight’ between two IPS officers

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

The confrontation occurred at an Assam Police battalion headquarters in the western part of the State on November 22, 2026

Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) downplayed an alleged clash between two senior Indian Police Service officers at a party as a “personal fight”.

The incident, involving a Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) and a Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), occurred at an Assam Police battalion in the western part of the State on Sunday night (November 22, 2026).

“There was a fight between two persons at a private programme. We have nothing to do here, as it was personal and had no connection with the Police Department. Sometimes, we also end up having arguments,” the Chief Minister told journalists on the sidelines of an official event.

“We would have done something had it happened during official duty. I have no comment on a personal matter,” he said.

According to reports, the DIG in question was among several senior police officers invited to a party the SSP had organised.

The DIG and the SSP allegedly quarrelled during the event. It turned physical, reportedly leaving the SSP injured.

Another senior IPS officer, reportedly assigned by Director General of Police Harmeet Singh, resolved the matter.

The trigger for the fight could not be ascertained. Police did not issue any statement.

articles.title: Juvenile Justice Board Hears Bail Plea of Child in Conflict with Law After High Court Rejection
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The High Court held that the CCL performed maneuvers with vehicles, posted videos on a page on Instagram, and operated vehicles without prioritizing safety, and that the parents knew of these acts but did not intervene

The Juvenile Justice Board is hearing a bail application under Section 12 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, submitted by a Child in Conflict with Law (CCL) concerning C.R. No.58/2026 at Tilak Nagar Police Station, which involves a collision on February 5, 2026, that caused death and disability, following orders from the Sessions Court and the Bombay High Court that cancelled bail and required placement in a centre for reformation.

The High Court held that the CCL performed maneuvers with vehicles, posted videos on a page on Instagram, and operated vehicles without prioritizing safety, and that the parents knew of these acts but did not intervene, leading the Sessions Court to set aside the bail order of March 6, 2026, on July 31, 2026, and the Bombay High Court to reject the revision on September 9, 2026, in Criminal Revision Application .

The Board noted an application dated October 21, 2026, where the CCL admitted that a paper presented as an examination timetable on October 9, 2026, did not belong to him because the paper contained subjects from a course under a scheme while the admission receipt of the CCL indicated enrollment in a course with a fee structure, and the confirmation for the paper came from the father of the CCL, who is a co-accused with a challenge to bail, and the Board had asked for confirmation on three occasions before receiving the confirmation from the father.

The report from the police stated that the CCL drove a KIA Seltos motorcar without a licence for driving and collided with a scooter on February 5, 2026, resulting in the death of Dhrumil Patel on February 15, 2026, and causing disability to the survivor, with the chargesheet filed on July 14, 2026, under Sections 281, 125, 125(A), 125(B) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, read with Sections 184 and 199 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1998, and Section 105 of the BNS.

The CCL argued that the investigation is complete and no recovery is pending, that the deletion of the account on Instagram is attributed to CCL No.2, that the meeting on February 8, 2026, involved mediators from the community and did not involve any attempt to withdraw the complaint, and that the conditions imposed by the Board did not prohibit entry into Ghatkopar, while the prosecution and the survivor argued that the CCL may contact individuals with records showing conviction, commit offenses, and pressurize witnesses, that the application seeks a review of the order from the High Court without a change in circumstances, and that the conduct of the CCL in evading the process and the submission of a paper that did not belong to the CCL does not support the grant of bail.

The CCL stated that the parents are ready to take responsibility for education, residence, and counseling, and the CCL completed the Higher Secondary Certificate Examination in the Commerce stream with a score of 74.83 percent and secured admission to the Bachelor of Commerce Programme for the year 2026-27 at KPB Hinduja College of Commerce. The survivor contended that the CCL did not comply with the directions of the Board, the CCL was not found at the address provided, the mother stated she did not know the whereabouts of the CCL, the father stated the CCL was at a location and did not produce the CCL on two occasions, and the CCL was produced on September 20, 2026, which the survivor stated was not a surrender without force.

articles.title: Human Metabolic Chamber inaugurated at CMC in Vellore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Human Metabolic Chamber is a room-sized calorimeter that measures oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production while a volunteer lives, eats, and sleeps inside for 24 hours or longer
A state-of-the-art Human Metabolic Chamber was inaugurated at Christian Medical College (CMC) in Vellore to advance research on nutrition, diabetes, obesity, and metabolic health.

According to a press release, the initiative was a joint collaboration of Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) and the CMC. The facility was opened by Punya Salila Srivastava, Union Secretary, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare.

The initiative brings together two of India’s premier institutions - combining TIFR’s strengths in fundamental and interdisciplinary science with CMC Vellore’s expertise in clinical medicine and metabolic research.

Anchored by TIFR’s Advanced Research Unit on Metabolism, Development & Aging (ARUMDA) and CMC’s Department of Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism, the collaboration will help address questions on how the body uses energy, and how this varies across diverse populations, diets, and lifestyles in India.

The chamber complements the National Analytical Facility for Nutrition and Metabolism Research, which ARUMDA established last year. Together, the two facilities allow researchers to link molecular and biochemical measurements with how the body uses energy. This ability to study metabolism at both levels places the initiative at the forefront of Indian research on metabolic diseases and aging.

The Human Metabolic Chamber is a room-sized calorimeter that measures oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production while a volunteer lives, eats, and sleeps inside for 24 hours or longer. These measurements reveal the total energy expenditure and how the body switches between using fat and carbohydrates across meals, activity, and sleep.

By analysing metabolism over an extended daily cycle, the chamber offers a more comprehensive picture than a brief measurement alone. It enables researchers to examine how energy use changes over time and under carefully defined study conditions. This capability is particularly important in India, whose diverse populations, dietary patterns, and lifestyles remain under-represented in global reference data.

Measurements generated through the facility can help refine the understanding of energy and nutrient requirements, and strengthen the evidence underpinning strategies against metabolic disease and malnutrition, the release said.

articles.title: Under Nishant’s leadership, the future of the party remains bright for next 30 years, says Sanjay Jha
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Jha also said that former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar has transformed Bihar’s image and identity over the past two decades.
Janata Dal (United) on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) celebrated Sushasan Diwas (Good governance Day) to mark the day Nitish Kumar began his first full term as the Bihar Chief Minister.

JD(U) National President Nitish Kumar also attended the main programme as a chief guest organised at the State headquarters office in Patna along with his son Nishant Kumar and Sanjay Jha, National Working president of the party.
Mr. Kumar also saw his sand art displayed in the office premises. Mr. Kumar was welcomed by party workers while showering rose petals on him.

Mr. Jha while addressing the party workers, said that the new generation needs to know what conditions were like in Bihar in 2005 and how Nitish Kumar ji worked to take the state forward, with good governance, development and social justice at the centre.
‘Nitish Samvad’ (Nitish Dialogue) events were also organized in every district where JD(U) leaders spoke about the works done by Mr. Kumar.

“Nitish Kumar ji will be remembered for his work for thousands of years. Bihar needed a leader who would understand its suffering, restore its lost dignity and take it forward on a new path of development. On November 24, 2005, a new era of good governance began in Bihar under the leadership of Nitish Kumar ji,”Mr. Jha said.

He further said, “The challenges Bihar faced before 2005 are no secret. From law and order to education, healthcare, roads and electricity, the state was in a worrying state on almost every measure of development. Even Biharis, living in other states, were reluctant to reveal their identity. But through his firm resolve, clear vision and systematic efforts, Nitish Kumar ji has transformed Bihar’s image and identity over the past two decades.”
Mr. Jha asserted that today, being called a Bihari is no longer an insult, but a source of pride and self-respect as Bihar has established a new identity for itself in many areas of development.
He also pointed out that the impact of Nitish Kumar work will endure for many generations to come.
“His presence will continue to inspire all of us to carry forward his commitment to building a developed, prosperous and self-reliant Bihar of his dreams,”Mr. Jha said.
Mr. Jha also said that Nitish Kumar brought the ideology of socialism into reality on the ground.
He explained that the Bhagalpur riots occurred during the rule of the Congress government, followed by 15 years of Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) rule, yet the victims never received justice.

articles.title: Bengal film fraternity members meet CM Suvendu Adhikari; demand more Bengali film screening
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Film fraternity members said regional Bengali language films were being sidelined because of national and international films
The West Bengal film fraternity members met with Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Tuesday (November 24) and demanded more Bengali film screenings at the cinema halls across the State.
Actors turned Bharatiya Janata Party MLAs Roopa Ganguly, Rudranil Ghosh, and others were present at the meeting.

“Today, we made a decision about Bengali films, to preserve the dignity and respect of regional Bengali culture, one Bengali film will have to be shown during prime time under any circumstances. Special care will be taken to ensure that Bengali films are not suddenly removed from the shows,” Mr Ghosh said.

Mr. Ghosh further added that new theatres will be built at 51 new locations. 70 old halls will also be converted into cinema halls to recover the conditions of the Bengali film industry. He further added that the CM has given a structured plan to ask producers, distributors, and other stakeholders to work together to better the condition of the industry.

Speaking to journalists after the meeting with the CM, Ms Ganguly also said, “There were many problems, and many of those problems are being resolved. Financial approval for many halls has also been given.”

“If we can all work together on all those things discussed with the CM today, then the face of the Bengali film industry will be completely different five years from now,” Bengali film producer Shrikant Mohta said. He added that the CM has shown commitment towards the Bengali film industry and has promised multiple steps to help change the situation on ground.
On Monday (November 23), the makers of new Bengali film “Sadhak Bamakhyapa” had raised concerns that they are not able to secure movie halls to screen their new film in theatres across the State.

“No other regional industry allows this where they push out their own language films to give space to English or Hindi films,” actor Saheb Chattopadhyay said about the distribution issue of the film. He said that he is not against any language films but that their own regional films should not be pushed out because of national and international films and everyone should get a fair chance to screen their cinema.
After the meeting with the Bengali film fraternity members, BJP WB page posted on their social media and announced that Sadhak Bamakhyapa will not be sidelined and be screened across the State.
“The Honourable Chief Minister Shri @SuvenduWB is leading the charge to celebrate and uplift Bengali cinema, language, and culture!” The BJP WB page said on their social media post.

The West Bengal film fraternity members met with Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Tuesday (November 24) and demanded more Bengali film screenings at the cinema halls across the State.

Actors turned Bharatiya Janata Party MLAs Roopa Ganguly, Rudranil Ghosh, and others were present at the meeting.

“Today, we made a decision about Bengali films, to preserve the dignity and respect of regional Bengali culture, one Bengali film will have to be shown during prime time under any circumstances. Special care will be taken to ensure that Bengali films are not suddenly removed from the shows,” Mr Ghosh said.

Mr. Ghosh further added that new theatres will be built at 51 new locations. 70 old halls will also be converted into cinema halls to recover the conditions of the Bengali film industry. He further added that the CM has given a structured plan to ask producers, distributors, and other stakeholders to work together to better the condition of the industry.

Speaking to journalists after the meeting with the CM, Ms Ganguly also said, “There were many problems, and many of those problems are being resolved. Financial approval for many halls has also been given.”

“If we can all work together on all those things discussed with the CM today, then the face of the Bengali film industry will be completely different five years from now,” Bengali film producer Shrikant Mohta said. He added that the CM has shown commitment towards the Bengali film industry and has promised multiple steps to help change the situation on ground.

On Monday (November 23), the makers of new Bengali film “Sadhak Bamakhyapa” had raised concerns that they are not able to secure movie halls to screen their new film in theatres across the State.

“No other regional industry allows this where they push out their own language films to give space to English or Hindi films,” actor Saheb Chattopadhyay said about the distribution issue of the film. He said that he is not against any language films but that their own regional films should not be pushed out because of national and international films and everyone should get a fair chance to screen their cinema.

After the meeting with the Bengali film fraternity members, BJP WB page posted on their social media and announced that Sadhak Bamakhyapa will not be sidelined and be screened across the State.

“The Honourable Chief Minister Shri @SuvenduWB is leading the charge to celebrate and uplift Bengali cinema, language, and culture!” The BJP WB page said on their social media post.

articles.title: Court rejects PG operator’s bail in Satya Niketan building collapse case, says he put profits above students’ lives
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘The accused persons, who are responsible for the loss of seven valuable lives, are not entitled to the benefit of discretion and such incidents must be dealt with by the courts of law with an iron hand,’ the court said

Observing that he appeared to have placed financial gains above the safety of students and labourers staying at the premises, a Delhi court on Monday refused to grant bail to Shubham Tyagi, one of operator of the paying guest (PG) accommodation in South Delhi’s Satya Niketan which collapsed in September this year leaving seven dead.

Additional Sessions Judge Dhirendra Rana of Patiala House Court denied bail to the accuse after rejecting Mr Tyagi’s argument that he had no responsibility for the construction of the PG which he has co-accused Sudhanshu Kumar had rented the property from its owners and operated a boy’s hostel.

It added that even if the construction was not being carried out under Mr Tyagi’s instructions, he was obligated to ensure that residents vacated the building until the work was completed. He was also expected to alert occupants about the potential structural danger.

“The accused persons, who are responsible for the loss of seven valuable lives, are not entitled to the benefit of discretion and such incidents must be dealt with by the courts of law with an iron hand,” court said.

Holding that Mr Tyagi could have anticipated the risks arising from alleged unauthorised construction and structural alterations court mentioned the statement of injured student Nitish Chhib, court said that it was alleged that basement construction had continued for 10-12 days despite complaints from students. The residents were allegedly threatened with eviction when they objected to the work.

Emphasising the gravity of the incident, the court observed that building collapses linked to illegal construction have repeatedly resulted in fatalities and must be treated seriously. It remarked that those allegedly responsible for the loss of seven lives did not deserve discretionary relief and that such incidents required a firm judicial response.
Denying bail, court also stated that the trial is at an early stage and public witnesses were yet to be examined and there was a possibility of witness intimidation.

The Delhi Police had filed a 638-page chargesheet in the matter earlier this month. It named building owner Hariram Gupta, his wife Urmila Gupta, their son Mahesh Gupta, labour contractor Sanoj Kumar and PG operators Mr Tyagi and Mr Kumar as accused.

articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.
Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return.
Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling.

“Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation.
“Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.”
The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23).
The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025.
Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.
The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

Neocloud and data-center companies, which came under sharp selling pressure earlier following Mr. Huang’s abrupt exit, also climbed. CoreWeave rose 21.5%, IREN gained 26.4% and Nebius advanced ⁠23.4%.
The S&P 500 information technology sector jumped 8.9% and led the gains in the benchmark index.

articles.title: Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: In a note accessed by The Hindu, the Ministry has said that the oil and gas industry has a long gestation period and so exploration and finance decisions taken more than a decade ago are affecting the industry now

The government expects domestic oil and gas production to pick up in the next 4-5 years as several steps taken in the recent past begin to bear fruit in an industry typically characterised by long gestation periods, The Hindu has learnt.
According to an analysis by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the current contraction in domestic oil and gas production is due to factors that took place more than a decade ago.

However, since then, the government has taken steps such as increasing drilling and exploration to record levels, changing laws and rules to provide stable terms to explorers, and opening new avenues for exploration.

“The steps taken in the last few years — new acreage, record drilling, deepwater wells and the revival of Mumbai High — will start showing up in production over the next three to four years,” the note asserted. “That is the nature of this sector: the decisions of one decade decide the output of the next.”
The note also argues that now, unlike earlier, the profits of oil and gas companies upstream companies like ONGC and Oil India are being used to fund exploration rather than subsidies.
“Until 2015, ONGC and Oil India were made to fund a large share of the subsidy on diesel, LPG and kerosene, through discounts on the crude they sold to oil marketing companies,” the note said.

According to data with the Ministry, ONGC paid ₹49,421 crore towards this subsidy in 2012-13 against a profit of ₹20,926 crore, and in 2013-14 paid ₹56,384 crore towards this subsidy against a net profit of ₹22,095 crore.

“In both years ONGC gave away more than twice what it earned,” the note said. “Money that should have gone into finding new oil and gas went into keeping retail prices down. This burden was ended from 2015-16. ONGC now keeps its earnings and has sharply raised its spending on exploration.”
According to the latest data on the Index of Core Industries, the oil and gas sectors have contracted continuously for 22 and 28 months, respectively.

“In this sector it takes five to ten years to go from awarding a block to first production,” a note prepared by the Ministry and accessed by The Hindu said. “Output in 2026 is the result of what was, and was not, done a decade ago.

“After the ninth New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP) round was launched in 2010, no new exploration round was offered until 2016,” it added. “The fields producing today were not replaced by new ones in that period, and the effect is still being felt.”

The Ministry also stated that mature oil and gas fields generally lose 7-8% of their output every year as reservoir pressure falls and that most of India’s current production comes from such fields. On the other hand, new wells, enhanced recovery, and field redevelopment are making up much of the loss.

articles.title: SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has retained State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank in its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), maintaining their respective positions under the same bucketing structure as in 2025.

Under the RBI’s framework, SBI, placed in Bucket 4, will have to maintain an additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital requirement of 0.80% of its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs). HDFC Bank, classified under Bucket 2, will have an additional CET1 requirement of 0.40%, while ICICI Bank, placed in Bucket 1, will have to maintain 0.20%.
These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks.

The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements.

The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance.

SBI and ICICI Bank were initially designated as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016, respectively. HDFC Bank joined the list in 2017, when all three banks were identified as systemically important financial institutions.

fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

articles.title: Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of livelihoods

While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery.

It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary.

“The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said.

“While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added.
He said that gold and jewellery hold a unique place in India’s cultural heritage, particularly during festive and wedding seasons, such as the period that India will soon enter in October-December.
“The jewellery industry, contributing nearly 7-8% to the economy and supporting millions of livelihoods, is an integral part of India’s growth story,” Mr. Rokde asserted.
‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal

“As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.

articles.title: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mikki Kivikoski said

“India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said.

"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI .

The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said.

"This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries.

The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May.

Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said.
The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges.

"What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

"There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.

Bilateral trade in goods and services between India and Finland stood at around $3.7 billion in 2025-26, marking a growth of about 25% over the previous year, and a 38.5% rise from $2.64 billion in 2021-22.
The startup event, Polar Bear Pitching, originated in Oulu, northern Finland, and has expanded internationally, connecting startups with investors and business networks.

articles.title: Israel’s Eisenkot clinches first coalition agreement in bid to form government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Yashar ​said that Mr. Eisenkot had met with Avigdor ⁠Lieberman, head of the Israel Our Home party, and they agreed on a deal afterward

Israel’s Yashar party, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot , said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) it agreed to ​sign a coalition pact with a right-wing Opposition party as it ‌seeks to form a government following last month’s election.

Yashar ​said that Mr. Eisenkot had met with Avigdor ⁠Lieberman, head of the Israel Our Home party, earlier on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) and they agreed on a deal afterward, the first such alliance since the election.

Israel’s ‌Parliament was sworn in on November 10 without a new government, after the election on October 27 stripped ‌Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority but left ‌others ⁠with no clear path to power.
President Isaac Herzog has ⁠tasked Eisenkot with forming a government, while Mr. Netanyahu remains caretaker Prime Minister.
Mr. Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud’s alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties outperformed election expectations but still lost its ​majority. It now holds 53 ‌of the Knesset’s 120 seats.

Mr. Eisenkot’s center-right Yashar party and patchwork coalition partners — including Mr. Lieberman — hold just 48 seats. But they have potential allies in the parties representing Israel’s Arab minority, which hold ‌19 seats and are aligned with Mr. Eisenkot in their ​vehement opposition to Mr. Netanyahu.

The agreement between Mr. Eisenkot, whose party won 21 parliament seats, and Mr. Lieberman, whose party ⁠won 7, was something of a surprise, since Mr. Lieberman had been vocal about his opposition to forming a government with support from ‌Arab parties as well as to a unity government with Mr. Netanyahu.
Mr. Lieberman has also said his main goal is to oust Mr. Netanyahu from power.

Mr. Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government under a 28-day mandate, but he could ask for a 14-day extension. If he fails, Mr. Netanyahu would get a shot. If ‌no one is able to form a government, another election will be held ​next year.
Talks are also ongoing between Mr. Eisenkot, some of his “change bloc” partners and Likud on forming a ⁠unity government.

The left-wing Democrats party, which won 8 parliamentary seats, separately said ⁠it was suspending talks with Mr. Eisenkot because of progress in his talks with Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud on a possible ‌unity government and “given with the deadlock in negotiations to form a ‘change government.’
Yair Golan, head of the Democrats, has said he ​prefers a government without Mr. Netanyahu but with Arab parties.

articles.title: Chinese tech giant Huawei is guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, U.S. jury finds
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Huawei was also accused of doing business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions, including Iran and North Korea, and making false statements to U.S. government officials and banks as part of an effort to hide its misdeeds

A U.S. jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud as it grew into one of the world's biggest suppliers of gear for wireless telecommunications networks.
However, jurors acquitted the company of the most serious charge it faced: engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy to steal intellectual property from American companies.
The verdict followed a lengthy trial in which U.S. prosecutors argued that Huawei repeatedly stole technological secrets from competitors and partners in the U.S. and elsewhere.

Huawei was also accused of doing business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions, including Iran and North Korea, and making false statements to U.S. government officials and banks as part of an effort to hide its misdeeds.

Lawyers for the company said U.S. investigators had used isolated episodes of wrongdoing by a few of Huawei's more than 200,000 employees to spin a false narrative about a grand conspiracy that didn't actually exist.

It's unclear what effect the verdict might have on Huawei's global fortunes. The company hasn't been allowed to sell equipment to U.S. carriers for years because of security concerns. It has also been blacklisted by other Western allies, including Canada and Britain.

That hasn't stopped the company from doing a robust business elsewhere. Its smartphones and other telecom equipment are sold globally. More recently, it has expanded into chipmaking as the boom in artificial intelligence fuels demand for microprocessors, becoming an important alternative in China to chips made by companies such as Nvidia.
The U.S. announced its criminal charges against Huawei in early 2019 and later expanded the allegations.
Chinese officials said the U.S. has engaged in “economic bullying” and improperly used national security as a pretext for oppressing Chinese companies.

The indictment against Huawei accused it of a long pattern of outright technology theft. Huawei, prosecutors said, once sold internet routers containing source code copied from a competitor. In another episode, a person working for Huawei slipped into a competitor's booth at a Chicago trade show to surreptitiously photograph the circuits inside another company's networking device, the indictment said. Prosecutors said that on another occasion, a Huawei worker removed a robotic arm from a competitor's lab so it could be photographed and measured.
The victim companies included Cisco Systems, Motorola Solutions, T-Mobile, Quintel USA and Fujitsu, according to court records.

“The tone was set at the top by Huawei leaders and executives who themselves engaged in criminal conduct, like lying to Congress, lying to banks, violating US sanctions and trying to interfere with the very criminal investigation that led to this case,” prosecutor Meredith Arfa told the jury at the trial.

🌐 International Affairs 📅 25 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Chinese tech giant Huawei is guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, U.S. jury finds

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics

Huawei was also accused of doing business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions, including Iran and North Korea, and making false statements to U.S. government officials and banks as part of an effort to hide its misdeeds

A U.S. jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud as it grew into one of the world's biggest suppliers of gear for wireless telecommunications networks.

However, jurors acquitted the company of the most serious charge it faced: engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy to steal intellectual property from American companies.

The verdict followed a lengthy trial in which U.S. prosecutors argued that Huawei repeatedly stole technological secrets from competitors and partners in the U.S. and elsewhere.

Huawei was also accused of doing business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions, including Iran and North Korea, and making false statements to U.S. government officials and banks as part of an effort to hide its misdeeds.

Lawyers for the company said U.S. investigators had used isolated episodes of wrongdoing by a few of Huawei's more than 200,000 employees to spin a false narrative about a grand conspiracy that didn't actually exist.

It's unclear what effect the verdict might have on Huawei's global fortunes. The company hasn't been allowed to sell equipment to U.S. carriers for years because of security concerns. It has also been blacklisted by other Western allies, including Canada and Britain.

That hasn't stopped the company from doing a robust business elsewhere. Its smartphones and other telecom equipment are sold globally. More recently, it has expanded into chipmaking as the boom in artificial intelligence fuels demand for microprocessors, becoming an important alternative in China to chips made by companies such as Nvidia.

The U.S. announced its criminal charges against Huawei in early 2019 and later expanded the allegations.

Chinese officials said the U.S. has engaged in “economic bullying” and improperly used national security as a pretext for oppressing Chinese companies.

The indictment against Huawei accused it of a long pattern of outright technology theft. Huawei, prosecutors said, once sold internet routers containing source code copied from a competitor. In another episode, a person working for Huawei slipped into a competitor's booth at a Chicago trade show to surreptitiously photograph the circuits inside another company's networking device, the indictment said. Prosecutors said that on another occasion, a Huawei worker removed a robotic arm from a competitor's lab so it could be photographed and measured.

The victim companies included Cisco Systems, Motorola Solutions, T-Mobile, Quintel USA and Fujitsu, according to court records.

“The tone was set at the top by Huawei leaders and executives who themselves engaged in criminal conduct, like lying to Congress, lying to banks, violating US sanctions and trying to interfere with the very criminal investigation that led to this case,” prosecutor Meredith Arfa told the jury at the trial.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “The tone was set at the top by Huawei leaders and executives who themselves engaged in criminal conduct, like lying to Congress, lying to banks, violating US sanctions and trying to interfere with the very criminal investigation that led to this case,” prosecutor Meredith Arfa told the jury at the trial.

articles.title: Malaysia to repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals despite ICJ genocide ruling
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Anwar Ibrahim told Parliament that Malaysia respected the ICJ’s ruling, but would continue to engage with Myanmar’s leadership to facilitate the repatriation of refugees

Malaysia will repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals next month, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as he defended the government's engagement with Myanmar's military leadership, despite a landmark international court ruling finding the country responsible for genocide against Rohingya Muslims.
Editorial | Just verdict: on Myanmar and the International Court of Justice

The International Court of Justice, based in The Hague, Netherlands, last week found Myanmar guilty of genocide against its Rohingya minority, with evidence showing Myanmar forces killed about 10,000 Rohingya in a 2017 military operation that included mass rapes and killings, and the destruction of thousands of homes.

Myanmar's government has dismissed the ruling as unfair. Mr. Anwar told Parliament that Malaysia respected the ICJ's ruling, but would continue to engage with Myanmar's leadership to facilitate the repatriation of refugees.

Malaysia hosts nearly 200,000 refugees from Myanmar, including Rohingya who fled a military crackdown and members of other ethnic minorities. Mr. Anwar said that efforts to resettle them in third countries had been unsuccessful and Malaysia couldn't continue bearing the burden indefinitely.
He said that talks with Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing, who visited Kuala Lumpur last month, had helped bring progress to the long-standing issue.
Another 1,500 people will be sent back on three Myanmar naval vessels on Dec. 6 and 7, while another 5,303 will return throughout next month by air, with all costs borne by Myanmar, Mr. Anwar said.
A total of 10,476 Myanmar nationals have already been repatriated this year, including 1,476 who were taken home aboard a Myanmar naval vessel on September 29, he said.
Malaysia had secured a guarantee of a “safe and dignified return” for those repatriated, Mr. Anwar said.
“So far, based on monitoring by Malaysian intelligence, none of the 10,476 individuals have been subjected to any form of pressure,” he said.

Despite the engagement with Myanmar, Mr. Anwar said that Malaysia remained committed to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations' peace plan to end violence and resolve a prolonged crisis in Myanmar after the military seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in 2021. It sparked widespread opposition that plunged large parts of the country into conflict.

The 11-nation regional bloc has renewed diplomatic pressure on Myanmar for failing to implement its peace initiative and restricted the country's top leaders from major regional summits. Myanmar has slammed ASEAN for unfair treatment.

articles.title: U.S. CIA, ODNI suffer cybersecurity breach of some unclassified information, NYT reports
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: While it was not clear specifically what unclassified material ​was compromised, information ‌at other government agencies was also believed to have been exposed in the breach

The U.S. Central Intelligence Agency ‌and the Office of the ​Director of National Intelligence recently ⁠discovered a cybersecurity breach that exposed some of their unclassified information, the New ‌York Times reported on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), citing people familiar with ‌the matter.
The intrusions affected a ‌network ⁠that looks for intelligence insights ⁠in public, unclassified material, the Times reported.
While it was not clear specifically what unclassified material ​was compromised, information ‌at other government agencies was also believed to have been exposed in the breach, the Times added.
Asked ‌about the report, the ODNI ​said there had been “no disruptions to critical capabilities or ⁠classified systems.” The CIA did not immediately respond to a request for ‌comment.

The news is the latest publicly reported hack in a series of tech outages and cybersecurity incidents, including a breach reported at the U.S. Department of Agriculture. Two separate ‌breaches have recently been disclosed at ​the FBI, while the Pentagon and the Department of Homeland ⁠Security have also been caught up in ⁠recent cyber incidents.

articles.title: Iran rules out talks with U.S. until its seven conditions are met
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Iran also said three oil tankers had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire despite U.S. aerial protection

Iran reiterated Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that it would not hold talks with the United States to end the conflict, saying that seven conditions must be met first, though it didn't specify the conditions.
Iran also said three oil tankers had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire despite U.S. aerial protection.
Meanwhile, at least nine Palestinians were killed in several Israeli strikes in Gaza, local officials said.

Iran's chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that Tehran wouldn't negotiate with the U.S. "until Iran's seven conditions are met,” according to Iranian state television.

Iranian authorities haven't publicly stated what those conditions are. But Iranian state media have said they include the lifting of sanctions, the ending of the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and the release of seized Iranian assets.
He also warned that Iran would “shift the geographical scope of the conflict should the enemy make a mistake.”
The naval arm of Iran's Revolutionary Guard said the three oil tankers struck the naval mines because they were “in violation of regulations” regarding passage through the Strait of Hormuz.
The Guard's navy said in a post on Telegram Monday (November 23, 2026) that the strait “is not a place to test unauthorised routes or to disregard maritime warnings.”
It said the tankers were “engulfed in flames” after hitting the mines despite being under U.S. aerial escort.

At least nine people were killed in four Israeli strikes Monday night (November 23, 2026) and Tuesday morning (November 24, 2026), officials in Gaza said. Among those killed was a senior security official in the Hamas-run government's Interior Ministry.

The ministry said Na'im Abu Nahl, director-general of its internal security service, was killed in a strike west of Gaza City on Tuesday (November 23, 2026). Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the killing and said Israel would continue targeting Hamas security forces.

Hospital officials across Gaza reported at least eight other deaths in four strikes, including a child killed in an airstrike in central Gaza on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) and three police officers killed in Khan Younis.

articles.title: Former members say EPG report was ‘highly positive’ for India-Nepal ties
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Their reaction comes a day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group “not relevant”

A day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of the India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group (EPG) “not relevant”, arguing that India will take a “forward looking” approach regarding boundary issues with Nepal, a former member of the EPG has said the report was “highly positive” for both India and Nepal and that it was “odd” that the group did not get a chance to present the report to the Government of India.

“The EPG report was produced after extensive research and field visits. We visited Visakhapatnam and other ports that are of interest to Nepal and spoke with many stakeholders before compiling the report and there are interesting recommendations in the report that could be of great use for India and Nepal and it was highly positive for Delhi-Kathmandu relations,” said Mahendra P. Lama, former professor of Jawaharlal Nehru University, who served as a member of the EPG.
ALSO WATCH India-Nepal ties: What does Modi-Balen partnership promise? | Above the Fold | Nov 23, 2026

The EPG returned to the spotlight on Monday (November 23, 2026) when Mr. Misri announced in a press conference held after the visit of Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah that New Delhi would adopt a “forward-looking” approach to the border issues. “The leaders have given a direction as part of the overall very forward-looking discussions that have been held today for the foreign secretaries to take the task forward. We will do so in a forward-looking manner, taking inspiration from the vision document and from the directions and indeed the spirit in which the discussions were held. I would say that EPG is in the past. We are not looking backward,” said Mr. Misri in response to a question. He described the EPG report as “not relevant”.

Former Nepali ambassador and coordinator of the EPG on the Nepali side, Bhek Bahadur Thapa, described the EPG report as a step forward for the bilateral consultation process. “It was not a unilateral document, it was a document created through bilateral consultation among experts appointed by New Delhi and Kathmandu,” said Mr. Thapa, who has also served as Foreign Minister of Nepal during 2004-05. The EPG report dealing with a broad spectrum of India-Nepal relations, including the Kalapani dispute and the 1950 India-Nepal Friendship Treaty was completed in 2018 but it remained under sealed covers. “It is odd that the report could not be launched here in Delhi. The Nepali side said the EPG report should be unveiled first by the Indian Prime Minister and on the same day we were supposed to return to Kathmandu for the report’s unveiling by the Nepali Prime Minister, “ said Prof. Lama, informing that they made a mistake as Kathmandu could have also unveiled the report first. “Our recommendations now can be accessed by other stakeholders in Kathmandu and I don’t think that is a positive thing,” said Mr. Lama.

The EPG was institutionalised according to an understanding that was reached during the delegation-level talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former Nepali Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli in February 2016. The visit of Mr. Oli took place against the backdrop of months-long blockade on Nepal-India border that Kathmandu said was imposed by India but India blamed the Madhesi agitators of Nepal for imposing the blockade that hindered flow of essential items such as cooking gas into Nepal. During the time of its existence, a part of the Institute of Defence Studies and Analyses (IDSA) in Delhi served as the secretariat for the EPG. The then Director General of the IDSA Jayant Prasad was also part of the EPG.

Incidentally, officials who are currently playing key roles in India-Nepal relations were also involved in the EPG process. Former members recounted that the newly appointed Indian ambassador to Nepal Sudhakar Dalela was the Joint Secretary (North) in the Ministry of External Affairs and was part of the EPG process during 2016-18. That apart, the new Nepali ambassador to India Nischal Nath Pandey also was part of the EPG process in Kathmandu.

We will do so in a forward-looking manner, taking inspiration from the vision document and from the directions and indeed the spirit in which the discussions were held. I would say that EPG is in the past. We are not looking backward,” said Mr. Misri in response to a question. He described the EPG report as “not relevant”.

Former Nepali ambassador and coordinator of the EPG on the Nepali side, Bhek Bahadur Thapa, described the EPG report as a step forward for the bilateral consultation process. “It was not a unilateral document, it was a document created through bilateral consultation among experts appointed by New Delhi and Kathmandu,” said Mr. Thapa, who has also served as Foreign Minister of Nepal during 2004-05. The EPG report dealing with a broad spectrum of India-Nepal relations, including the Kalapani dispute and the 1950 India-Nepal Friendship Treaty was completed in 2018 but it remained under sealed covers. “It is odd that the report could not be launched here in Delhi. The Nepali side said the EPG report should be unveiled first by the Indian Prime Minister and on the same day we were supposed to return to Kathmandu for the report’s unveiling by the Nepali Prime Minister, “ said Prof. Lama, informing that they made a mistake as Kathmandu could have also unveiled the report first. “Our recommendations now can be accessed by other stakeholders in Kathmandu and I don’t think that is a positive thing,” said Mr. Lama.

The EPG was institutionalised according to an understanding that was reached during the delegation-level talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former Nepali Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli in February 2016. The visit of Mr. Oli took place against the backdrop of months-long blockade on Nepal-India border that Kathmandu said was imposed by India but India blamed the Madhesi agitators of Nepal for imposing the blockade that hindered flow of essential items such as cooking gas into Nepal. During the time of its existence, a part of the Institute of Defence Studies and Analyses (IDSA) in Delhi served as the secretariat for the EPG. The then Director General of the IDSA Jayant Prasad was also part of the EPG.

Incidentally, officials who are currently playing key roles in India-Nepal relations were also involved in the EPG process. Former members recounted that the newly appointed Indian ambassador to Nepal Sudhakar Dalela was the Joint Secretary (North) in the Ministry of External Affairs and was part of the EPG process during 2016-18. That apart, the new Nepali ambassador to India Nischal Nath Pandey also was part of the EPG process in Kathmandu.

articles.title: Indian space companies sign largest-of-its-kind deal on satellite systems
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Bellatrix Aerospace to supply in-space propulsion systems for GalaxEye’s 30 satellites

Indian space companies GalaxEye and Bellatrix Aerospace on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) signed a multi-year contract in which Bellatrix Aerospace will supply in-space propulsion systems for the next 30 satellites GalaxEye is building.

This made the deal the “largest business-to-business order” one Indian private space company has placed with another since the space sector opened to private players in 2020, a press release noted. While private companies have participated in India’s space sector since inception, it has usually been as suppliers to the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).
The GalaxEye-Bellatrix deal was unveiled at the 5th India International Space Conclave, organised by the Indian Space Association (ISpA). The financial details of the contract were not disclosed.

GalaxEye is building the world’s first OptoSAR satellite constellation. OptoSAR is a proprietary imaging technology that allows customers to see any place on Earth through clouds, smoke, and darkness. Bellatrix builds the thrusters that steer and position satellites once they reach orbit, with hardware already flight-tested on ISRO missions.

“OptoSAR satellites are demanding customers. They need precise, repeatable orbits across a whole constellation, not a single demonstration. Our thrusters have already fired in orbit on ISRO missions, and we have built the production lines to deliver that same performance at constellation scale,” Rohan M. Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of Bellatrix Aerospace, said in a statement. Bellatrix makes electric and green propulsion systems for satellites and orbital transfer vehicles.

Mission Drishti, launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 on May 3, 2026, became the world’s first OptoSAR satellite in orbit. It validated GalaxEye’s spacecraft deployment, attitude control, onboard computing and in-house mission operations before contact was lost after a geomagnetic storm, the company stated.

In September, the Department of Science and Technology’s Technology Development Board committed ₹63.84 crore from the Government of India’s Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund for GalaxEye’s next multi-sensor satellite, which targets imagery sharper than 0.5 metres. Sourcing propulsion from a partner in the same city gives GalaxEye closer engineering control and shorter lead times as it builds that satellite.
“Drishti taught us that every critical system on a satellite has to be one we can see, test and improve up close,” Suyash Singh, co-founder and CEO of GalaxEye, said in a statement.

ISRO chairman V. Narayanan said that private industry was now indispensable to India’s space ecosystem. “Today, we are extremely happy that 440 start-up companies are working in the space area. Whenever a launch vehicle lifts off or we place a satellite, 70-80% of the budget is pumped into the Indian industry. Without the support of Indian industry, we would not have reached the present level.”

Other officials, however, pointed out while India was putting in place a system to increase capacity, it had to work towards increasing demand for products from the private space ecosystem. “The first phase of India’s space reforms opened the sector and created an institutional framework for private participation. Now India has to work on generating heavy demand. I have less concern about capacity being created; I see a bigger need for demand to be created. The second is to have enough money coming into the sector, and number three, to have procedures at all levels. Space is not a sector that is going to give you a payback in six months or nine months. Perseverance is required, and the government must continue to have policy stability,” said Pawan Goenka, chairman, InSpace, India’s single-window regulatory and promotional body for the private space sector.
