articles.title: Thirupparankundram 'deepathoon' row LIVE: Tamil Nadu BJP chief arrested, tight security in hillock on Karthigai Deepam day
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: An interim order allowing lamp lighting on the 'deepathoon' just one time, a review petition pending hearing, and a security blanket around the hill town amid the festival of lights. All eyes are on Thirupparankundram

Nainar Nagenthran, who left his home in Tirunelveli district at 2.35 pm for Thirupparankundram, was arrested at Thatchanallur check-post on Tirunelveli City outskirts at 3.15 pm along with a group of party functionaries.

Police team led by Assistant Commissioner of Police, Palayamkottai, Rajamurali Ramachandran has been deployed in front of the house of Mr. Nagenthran to stop him from going to Thirupparankundram to participate in Karthigai Deepam festival.
Here’s a look at the history and legal background of this long-running dispute.

When a row broke out over lighting of Karthigai Deepam at the hill in Madurai, four Sthaneeka Bhattars of the Subramaniaswami Temple testified that the lamp had been lit at the Uchipillaiyar Temple since “time immemorial”
The Bhattars conveyed this in a communication written to the temple authorities against the backdrop of a raging row over the Hindu Munnani’s demand for lighting the deepam at a different place.
Thirupparankundram deepam row: what Sthaneeka Bhattars testified 30 years ago

In Thirupparankundram in Madurai, Hindus and Muslims live in camaraderie, but that has not kept the hill, which holds a couple of temples, a dargah, and some Jain beds, out of dispute. Here, we outline the history of judgments involving different petitioners through the years, in an attempt to understand the current crisis.
Thirupparankundram row: when politics invades a syncretic hill town
Madurai city police have declared Thirupparankundram hill and its surroundings a ‘Red Zone,’ imposing a complete ban on the operation of drones and unmanned aerial vehicles.

The heightened security measures come against the backdrop of intense legal and political developments surrounding the lighting of the ceremonial lamp on the ‘deepathoon’ atop the Thirupparankundram hill.

As a precautionary measure amid the ‘deepathoon’ row, devotees are not being allowed to climb the Thirupparankundram hill to offer worship at either the Kasi Viswanathar temple or the Sikandar Badhusha dargah.

Only those identified by the administration to witness the lighting of the lamp on the deepathoon, a newly designated spot, in accordance with the Supreme Court’s directions, will be allowed to climb the hillock, a police officer told The Hindu.

articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.
Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return.
Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling.

“Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation.
“Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.”
The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23).
The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025.
Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.
The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

Neocloud and data-center companies, which came under sharp selling pressure earlier following Mr. Huang’s abrupt exit, also climbed. CoreWeave rose 21.5%, IREN gained 26.4% and Nebius advanced ⁠23.4%.
The S&P 500 information technology sector jumped 8.9% and led the gains in the benchmark index.

articles.title: Iran carries out flogging of singer and her team, Iranian website says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Parastoo Ahmadi and the four others ‌were also handed two-year bans on artistic and musical activities and ‌travel, Emtedad website quoted lawyer ‌Mostafa ⁠Nili as saying

An Iranian singer and four members of her production ​team have each received 74 lashes after being ‌sentenced for "offending public decency by ​producing and publishing obscene and ⁠immoral content online", an Iranian news website said on Monday (November 23, 2026).
Parastoo Ahmadi and the four others ‌were also handed two-year bans on artistic and musical activities and ‌travel, the Emtedad website quoted lawyer ‌Mostafa ⁠Nili as saying.

The case ⁠followed the release of a video on YouTube in December 2024 showing Ms. Ahmadi performing without the ​mandatory hijab alongside male ‌musicians in Qom, south of the capital Tehran, Norway-based human rights group Hengaw said.

Western governments and human rights ‌groups have criticised flogging as torture ​and a violation of international law. Iran rejects accusations over its ⁠human rights record, saying Western countries should focus on their own human rights ‌problems.
Iranian authorities did not immediately respond to a request for comment by Reuters.

Rules requiring women to wear the hijab were a flashpoint during protests in 2022 after the death ‌in custody of Kurdish Iranian woman Mahsa Amini, ​who was arrested for allegedly violating the dress code.
The rules have increasingly ⁠been flouted on the streets of Tehran ⁠and beyond, and enforcement of the rules has also become more ‌selective.
Emtedad did not specify whether Mr. Nili had represented the five defendants.

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina could only be brought back to Bangladesh in handcuffs: Humaiun Kobir
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance,” Bangladesh State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir

Deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina could only be brought back to Bangladesh in handcuffs or under strict surveillance, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), according to a local media report.
Ms. Hasina, 79, has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh on August 5, 2024, following a student-led protest that toppled her government.
Bangladesh has been seeking her extradition from India, while New Delhi has maintained that Dhaka's extradition request was being examined through a legal process.

Ms. Hasina’s spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali, speaking to a news agency on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), said she would return on December 16, which Bangladesh celebrates as Victory Day to commemorate independence from Pakistan after the 1971 war.
Ms. Hasina has urged Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her return on the national airline.
“Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” the spokesman said.
Responding to the news report, Mr. Kobir said, “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance."
"A distinction had to be drawn between what Hasina wanted and what could happen," he was quoted as saying by the state-run BSS news agency.

The issue of Ms. Hasina's return has emerged as a major source of tension between Dhaka and New Delhi, with the latest wave of unrest in Bangladesh following the government's rejection of her request for a fresh passport and national identity card earlier this month.
Ms. Hasina's lawyers had approached the Bangladesh mission in New Delhi seeking the documents to facilitate her planned return in December.

Dhaka has insisted that Ms. Hasina, who was sentenced to death in absentia in November 2025 for crimes against humanity over the 2024 crackdown on protesters, must be brought back from India under a bilateral extradition treaty rather than allowed to return as an ordinary traveller.
Ms. Hasina has said she intends to return to Bangladesh on her own and surrender before a court. She has denied the charges against her.

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from exile on December 16, spokesperson says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Ms. Hasina went into exile in India on August 5, 2024, after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule

Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from exile in India on December 16, the day the country celebrates as Victory Day when it won independence after a war with Pakistan.

Ms. Hasina went into exile in India on August 5, 2024, after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule. She was sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity involving the uprising in which hundreds of protesters were killed. Ms. Hasina rejected the verdict and has said she is ready fight the case once she is back.
In the statement on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) announcing the planned date of her return, she urged current Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her return on the national airline.

“Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali said in the statement.

“It is deeply symbolic that she has chosen 16 December, our Victory Day, for her planned return to Bangladesh. We firmly believe that she will celebrate this historic day among her people, honoring the great victory achieved under the leadership of her father, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman,” Abu Obaidha Arin, an aide to Ms. Hasina, told The Associated Press .
“We are equally confident that, she will definitely return and under her leadership post return, Bangladesh will once again advance towards peace, stability and prosperity,” Mr. Arin said.
Earlier this month, in an interview with The Associated Press , Ms. Hasina said she would return to the country in December at any cost, and even death could not prevent her from returning home.

articles.title: How Herat defied the Taliban regime, chanting ‘women, work and freedom’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The protests in the Afghan city in the first week of June were triggered by the enforcement of a dress code, which requires women to wear burqa in public; many women, including those wearing traditional Afghan wear of manto, were arrested, but released later as entire communities protested
The chants were familiar. But this time, they echoed not in Tehran, but in Herat.

In mid-June, Afghanistan’s western city of Herat witnessed a rare display of public defiance against the Taliban. Women, and this time, men too, marched through the streets chanting “Women, Work and Freedom”, a slogan probably inspired by Iran’s 2022 “Woman, Life and Freedom” movement that emerged after the death of the 22-year-old Mahsa Amini.

According to Zan Times , an exiled media organisation run by Afghan women journalists, the latest crackdown appears to have been planned days in advance. On June 4, Herat’s governor Noor Ahmad Islamjar reportedly met with a group of morality enforcers.

On the afternoon of June 5, Taliban officials used the end of Friday prayers to announce that women who failed to comply with the Islamic dress code would be arrested. The following morning, the arrests began.

articles.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime.

The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels. The EU’s stance was reportedly supported by about 130 countries.

On the other side of the divide, India is among the nations that supported the proposed cover text, as they want to keep using fossil fuels for the foreseeable future, with Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav stressing that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation.”

“We express profound disappointment with the final draft COP31 cover decision or Antalya Pact. At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short,” Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said, speaking on behalf of the EU.

“We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach… We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” he added.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome, it needs the consensus of all parties.

Panama also formally objected to the text, saying that as a country battling droughts and other perilous impacts of climate change, the lack of any commitment to keep the rise in temperatures below 1.5 degrees C with firm action on phasing out fossil fuels was “a setback”.

“Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it weighs too much upon technologies such as CCUS [carbon capture utilisation and storage] instead of calling for deep changes, and three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator.

On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against language on prescriptive fossil fuel targets and didn’t oppose the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

Amandeep Garg, who was leading India’s delegation but speaking in his capacity as a spokesperson on behalf of the LMDC, said on the floor: “Everyone has worked tirelessly, and despite our discomfort with some elements of the text, we are willing to move forward, and continue to engage.” The LMDC expressed “concern” about the principles of equity and common but differentiated responsibility not being adequately reflected, adding that there was a “dilution” of the principle of developed countries taking historical responsibility and meeting their obligations.

“At the threshold of crossing 1.5 deg. C, we have raised a fundamental point – we need to reflect why we are here. Whose emissions, both past and continuing, have exhausted the global carbon budget? The cover decision does not reflect this, and only repeats agreed paragraphs from previous decisions to reflect responsibility and does not connect this with the imminent prospect of exceeding 1.5 deg. C,” he said.

This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator.

On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against language on prescriptive fossil fuel targets and didn’t oppose the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

Amandeep Garg, who was leading India’s delegation but speaking in his capacity as a spokesperson on behalf of the LMDC, said on the floor: “Everyone has worked tirelessly, and despite our discomfort with some elements of the text, we are willing to move forward, and continue to engage.” The LMDC expressed “concern” about the principles of equity and common but differentiated responsibility not being adequately reflected, adding that there was a “dilution” of the principle of developed countries taking historical responsibility and meeting their obligations.

“At the threshold of crossing 1.5 deg. C, we have raised a fundamental point – we need to reflect why we are here. Whose emissions, both past and continuing, have exhausted the global carbon budget? C,” he said.

articles.title: De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlapping procedures, but will it safeguard standards of medical education?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Under MSMER-2023, there was a defined escalation path; now, action depends on MARB assessments being initiated, completed and acted upon within a reasonable timeframe

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has de-notified and withdrawn the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 (MSMER-2023) where medical colleges were liable to face penalty fines for violations of educational standards and infrastructure requirements at medical colleges.

Earlier reports in The Hindu stated NMC’s withdrawal of MSMER-2023 weakens accountability in medical education by removing provisions to fine individual faculty members and administrators up to ₹5 lakh for submitting false information. Although the Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) can still penalise institutions up to ₹1 crore under separate regulations, institutional penalties may be less effective in deterring individual misconduct. Misleading faculty declarations, inflated patient records, or inadequate clinical training going undetected could ultimately put patients at risk.

The NMC justified the withdrawal by arguing that MSMER created overlapping assessment powers with MARB. However, scrapping the regulations entirely raises questions about the necessity of this move, particularly when non-compliance remains common and transparency in medical education is inadequate. Moreover, conflicting appeal deadlines under MARB regulations and the NMC Act could lead to legal disputes and delay enforcement. Ultimately, the NMC must clarify whether the existing regulatory mechanisms are being effectively enforced and whether their outcomes are publicly accessible without which the withdrawal of MSMER risks appearing to be a relaxation of regulatory oversight rather than a simplification of rules.

Medical experts have further warned that deterrence against practices such as ghost faculty and fabricated patient records would potentially expose students and institutions to greater malpractice and mismanagement. While some experts support the removal of regulatory duplication, they emphasise that effective oversight depends on rigorous verification, transparent reporting, consistent penalties and time-bound enforcement. The NMC must therefore demonstrate that MARB can enforce standards as effectively as the withdrawn framework; otherwise, regulatory rationalisation risks becoming a dilution of accountability.

The NMC has clarified that the MSMER introduced a parallel mechanism through which the undergraduate and postgraduate boards could assess institutions, thereby encroaching on the MARB’s mandate. While talking to The Hindu , NMC officials said the denotification is aimed at simplifying regulatory procedures and eliminating overlapping responsibilities, without compromising the quality of medical education.

articles.title: Webinar on autoimmune conditions to be held on November 28
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The webinar will examine how autoimmune conditions develop, their common symptoms, the challenges in diagnosis, and current approaches to treatment and long-term management
The Hindu will conduct a free health webinar on Saturday, November 28, 2026, on the topic ‘Understanding Autoimmune Conditions’. The webinar will be held from 11.30 a.m. to 12.30 p.m.

Autoimmune conditions occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body’s own tissues and organs. These disorders can affect different parts of the body, including the joints, skin, nervous system and other organs, and may present with a wide range of symptoms.

The session will explore how autoimmune conditions develop, the role of the immune system, and the common signs and symptoms associated with these disorders. It will also discuss early warning signs, including persistent fatigue, joint pain, muscle weakness and neurological symptoms, and explain when these warrant medical attention.

The discussion will examine the challenges involved in diagnosing autoimmune conditions, the role of clinical evaluation and diagnostic tests, and the treatment options available. The panellists will also discuss long-term disease management, monitoring, and the importance of timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment.

Expert panellists include Aishwarya G., Consultant Rheumatologist and Clinical Immunologist, Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Chennai. She will discuss the immune mechanisms underlying autoimmune conditions, common rheumatological disorders, their symptoms, diagnostic approaches and current treatment options.

The panel will also feature Prabash Prabhakaran, Director and Senior Consultant – Neurology, SIMS Hospital, Vadapalani, Chennai. He will discuss autoimmune conditions affecting the nervous system, the neurological symptoms they can cause, approaches to diagnosis and treatment, and the importance of recognising neurological manifestations.
The session will be moderated by Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu .

articles.title: Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO: 6 CEOs who reclaimed their top positions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had resigned due to an alleged Chinese spy scandal on November 12, 2026.

Jensen Huang, co-founder of Nvidia, who had stepped down as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the chipmaker, was re-instated in the top job on November 23, 2026. Mr Huang had resigned due to an alleged Chinese spy scandal on November 12, and CFO Colette Kress was appointed as interim CEO.

The board voted unanimously to bring Mr Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead”, Nvidia said in a statement.
Huang’s return has put the spotlight on the ouster and return of other top bosses. Here’s a look at some of the major names.
Former Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey | Photo Credit: Sandeep Saxena

The return of Mr Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia is unique, as reports suggest that senior U.S. government officials left the company’s board confident that he posed no national security risk amid concerns of China vying for the company’s advanced chips. U.S. President Donald Trump also welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.” I believe my ​intervention was very important to get Jensen Huang back,” Mr Trump told CNBC after Mr Huang’s reinstatement, marking an unprecedented intervention by U.S. government officials into the matters of a publicly traded company.

articles.title: GTA VI is here, and India has taken the day off
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru

This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. It is a very 2026 way to launch a game, and an apt one, given that Grand Theft Auto has always found its way to Indian players through whichever door happened to be open.

The game itself costs ₹5,999 for the Standard Edition and ₹7,499 for the Ultimate Edition on both PlayStation and Xbox, which is almost exactly double what Grand Theft Auto V cost here at launch. In dollars, though, Indian buyers pay about US$63 for the Standard Edition versus the $79.99 charged in the United States, and pre-order customers also receive the Vintage Vice City Pack. It is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only for now, with no PC version announced, which is a shift for a series so many Indians first met on a computer, though Grand Theft Auto V took the same route and reached PC in 2015.

In solidarity, consumer electronics brand boAt offered employees an optional day off on November 19, announcing it with the caption Out of office. Into Vice City. In Chennai, interior design firm Inde by ChairsCarte declared a holiday for its staff, interns and freelancers, calling it “just a day off for a game we’ve waited years for”.

For a generation of Indian players, the first port of call was the neighbourhood cyber café. Vice City and San Andreas, which defined the series in the early 2000s, were among the first open worlds many Indians explored, playing on rented computers by the hour, often between rounds of Counter-Strike, long before gaming became a career in India. San Andreas also gave us cheat codes, strings of nonsense such as HESOYAM, which replenished health, armour and cash in one go. For those who grew up typing them, they remain shorthand for nostalgia.

Even Indians who have never owned a copy know the series, thanks to its meme culture. The grey-and-red Wasted screen from GTA V, which appears when a character dies, has spent years slapped onto videos of people and animals spectacularly failing at something. Big Smoke’s exasperated yell at CJ for losing a train in San Andreas became so widely shared that Rockstar later named a GTA V trophy Better Than CJ in its honour. But the longest-running joke was about the wait. As the sequel failed to materialise, “We got X before GTA 6” became the Internet’s way of reacting to anything improbable. India took to it enthusiastically, with electronics retailer Croma fuelling another round when the game was delayed to November 19, 2026.

fullParagraphs: India stopped collecting anaemia data as part of NFHS, after the 5th round. This is the first time anaemia data is being published, after the measure was withdrawn from the NFHS on the grounds that the government intended to conduct a gold-standard test of drawing venous blood, instead of the finger prick test

Data put out by the Ministry of health and Family Welfare as per the latest SAMPADA (Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry), claims a drop in prevalence of anaemia levels across age and gender groups. Among children, it has dropped to 41.8 %, as against the previous figure from National Family Health Survey-5 data of 64%; among women it has dropped to 56% from 57%, and in pregnant women, the current survey puts it at 44% (down from 52%). articles.title: T.N. BJP chief Nainar Nagenthran arrested in Tirunelveli while heading to Thirupparankundram
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: When Nagenthran started his journey to Thirupparankundram from his house at 2.35 p.m., the police followed him; as his car reached the Thatchanallur check-post, they arrested him

BJP State president Nainar Nagenthran was arrested on the outskirts of Tirunelveli on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) for defying police instructions and attempting to travel to Thirupparankundram to witness the ‘Karthigai Deepam’ festival, where the Madurai district administration had clamped prohibitory orders.

Along with BJP cadres, he was taken to a nearby marriage hall. “The police, who were waiting in front of my house in Perumalpuram since morning, did not allow me to leave my house. Even when I went out to drop my granddaughter at school, the police followed me. Now, I have been arrested as I was going to Thirupparankundram to witness the lighting of the ‘Deepam’ on the pillar atop the hillock,” Mr. Nagenthran said, while he was being taken to the marriage hall.

At his residence in Perumalpuram earlier in the day, Mr. Nagenthran told reporters that Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay should ensure the lighting of the ‘Karthigai Deepam’ atop the pillar as directed by the Supreme Court on this auspicious day . He alleged that although Mr. Vijay visited the Mookambika temple and carried a spear during his visits to Murugan temples, the obstacles he was creating to the lighting of the ‘Karthigai Deepam’ atop the pillar had exposed his true beliefs. Hence, his government was describing the ‘deepa thoon’ as a ‘survey stone’ , the BJP leader charged.

#ThirupparankundramDeepam row: #TamilNadu #BJP president #NainarNagenthran was arrested by police at Thatchanallur in #Tirunelveli when he was proceeding to #Thirupparankundram on Tuesday afternoon. 📹&📸: A. Shaikmohideen (@photoshaik69) / The Hindu https://t.co/heos9GV0TT

“There is no sign of the Tamil Nadu government complying with this [SC] order. Lighting of the ‘Karthigai Deepam’ atop the pillar is the demand and desire of the majority community. If not, we’ll have to understand that he [Mr. Vijay] has absolute contempt for the apex court’s direction or that the Chief Minister does not know anything about administration,” he said.

When asked if he had been kept under ‘house arrest’, Mr. Nagenthran replied: “You have to ask this question of the police, who are unnecessarily creating tension across the State through heavy deployment in front of the houses of the leaders of the BJP and the Hindu outfits”.

He said an announcement by the Tamil Nadu government that the Madurai District Collector-led team would light the ‘Karthigai Deepam’ on the pillar atop the Thirupparankundram hillock would douse the tension instantly. “Instead, the government is triggering tension by heavily deploying police everywhere. The Joseph Vijay-led government is worse than the previous DMK government,” charged Mr. Nagenthran, who spoke freely with reporters and BJP workers who came to his house.

When Mr. Nagenthran started his journey to Thirupparankundram from his house at 2.35 p.m., the police followed him, while BJP cadres also followed his vehicle in cars and on bikes. As his car reached the Thatchanallur check-post, the northern boundary of Tirunelveli City Police jurisdiction, at 3.15 p.m., the police intercepted and arrested him.

articles.title: CJP won't stand with any political party in upcoming UP elections, says Abhijeet Dipke
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Abhijeet Dipke expressed hope that elections will be youth-centric and not tied to caste and religion
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) will neither contest elections nor support any political party in the upcoming Uttar Pradesh polls, CJP convenor Abhijeet Dipke said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).
He expressed hope that elections will be youth-centric and not tied to caste and religion.

"We are not going to get into elections. But the elections should take place on the issues of youth. How long are we going to contest on caste and religion? The world is discussing AI and renewable energy," Mr. Dipke told reporters in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.
CJP launches Cockroach Club to shift ‘youth movement beyond street protests’
When asked about the political scenario in Uttar Pradesh, Mr. Dipke said the CJP will not stand with any party.
"We won't speak about who should form the Government and who should not. We want national politics to focus on employment and quality education," he added.

articles.title: Sprouted dal, not maggots: BIAL clarifies allegations regarding meal served at Bengaluru airport’s 080 International Lounge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: BIAL has said that an internal review and kitchen inspection was conducted and it found that the dish was prepared using sprouted dal, and the appearance of the cooked germinated lentil may have been mistaken for a foreign object.

Responding to a post on X that maggots were reportedly found in a meal served at the Kempegowda International Airport’s (KIA) 080 International Lounge, the Bangalore International Airport Limited (BIAL) has clarified that the object found was sprouted dal.

A Bengalurean, Rajiv Tiwari, had posted on X that prior to boarding a flight to Germany from the Terminal-2 of KIA, his daughter had ordered a meal at the 080 International Lounge and found maggots in them.

“Maggots found in food at the 080 International Lounge, T2 Bengaluru Airport, right before my daughter’s flight to Germany. She ate some before realizing it was spoilt. Unacceptable hygiene! @BLRAirport @fssaiindia must inspect immediately, Mr.Tiwari posted from his X handle @RajivT1311 on November 23.

Maggots found in food at the 080 International Lounge, T2 Bengaluru Airport, right before my daughter's flight to Germany. She ate some before realizing it was spoilt. Unacceptable hygiene! @BLRAirport @fssaiindia must inspect immediately. Photos attached. https://t.co/O9Jrvp0oaP

In response to this BIAL has said that an internal review and kitchen inspection was conducted and it found that the dish was prepared using sprouted dal, and the appearance of the cooked germinated lentil may have been mistaken for a foreign object.

“We acknowledge the concern raised regarding a meal served at BLR Airport’s 080 International Lounge. Following an internal review and kitchen inspection, it was found that the dish had been prepared using sprouted dal, and the appearance of the cooked germinated lentil may have been mistaken for a foreign object,” BIAL said.

“The well-being of our passengers remains our highest priority. We uphold stringent quality and hygiene standards through regular audits and checks, and will continue to ensure that established food safety and hygiene protocols are consistently maintained,” it further added.

articles.title: After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hails the move as ‘putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first’

Six years after parting ways because of differences over the three farm laws, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its oldest ally, the Shiromani Akali Dali (SAD ), reunited ahead of the Assembly election in Punjab, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailing the move as “putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first”.

The announcement of the return of the SAD to the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) headed by the BJP was made at a press conference held at the BJP’s headquarters in New Delhi, and addressed by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, and BJP president Nitin Nabin.

Seat adjustment details are yet to be ironed out, according to Mr. Nabin, who said talks in this regard were ongoing, while Mr. Shah clarified that the SAD would continue to hold the status of “elder brother” or the more dominant partner in the State, with a claim to the Chief Minister’s post if the alliance came to power. “It is usually the elder brother who has a claim to the CM’s post,” Mr. Shah said.
The alliance’s goal was to make Punjab drug-free by December 31, 2029, and make sure that law and order, development, and issues pertaining to farmers were addressed, the Home Minister also said.

Mr. Badal hailed the long history and personal equations between senior leaders of the BJP, the late former PM Atal Behari Vajpayee and L.K. Advani, with his own father, late CM of Punjab, Parkash Singh Badal, who had, between the three of them, fashioned the alliance in 1996.

“This is not a political alliance; it’s an alliance of people’s sentiments,” Mr. Sukhbir Badal said, emphasising Hindu- Sikh unity and harmony, as did Mr. Nabin in his remarks. The PM would be attending a public meeting in Moga on December 8, Mr. Sukhbir Badal said, marking the birth anniversary of Parkash Singh Badal.

VIDEO | Delhi: During a joint press conference, Union Home Minister Amit Shah (@AmitShah) says, "BJP, the Akali Dal, and the NDA will contest in Punjab, and we will announce several key points in our manifesto. But, I want to make one thing very clear: eliminating drugs from Punjab will be our primary goal, eliminating corruption in Punjab will be our primary goal, and strengthening nationalist forces in Punjab will also be our primary goal. The current government in the state, led by Kejriwal Ji, had come to power promising to eliminate drugs within three months. They promised to eliminate drugs, but the problem has not been eradicated; it has increased. In 2017, Rahul Gandhi Ji had promised that drugs would be eliminated within one term. He made that promise, but his party also did nothing to address the drug problem. Now, I want to reiterate a promise that I made there: by December 31, 2029, we will make Punjab completely drug-free." (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd)

While the contours of the exact seat-sharing agreement are yet to be decided, in the past, the BJP contested 23 out of the 117 seats in the fray, a situation that is likely to change, with the BJP being given more seats, albeit still fewer than the SAD.

The alliance had won 93 seats in the 1997 Assembly election, with the SAD winning 75 seats and the BJP winning 18 seats. After losing power to the Congress in 2002, the alliance returned to office in 2007 with 68 seats and retained power in 2012 with an identical tally, bucking Punjab’s trend of voting out incumbent governments.

The SAD walked away from the NDA in 2020, with party MP Harsimrat Badal also resigning her position as Minister in the Modi government at the Centre over the three farm laws that sought to re-engineer agri-commerce, igniting months-long protests on Delhi’s borders. To a question by the media on what the SAD had to say about the farm laws now, Mr. Shah answered that since the farm Bills had been withdrawn by the government, “there is no point in asking the question”.

Mr. Modi had pushed for the alliance, for both sentiment and realpolitik, sources in the know said. “The sentiments with regard to the Sikh community, and an alliance of parties appealing to both Hindu and orthodox Sikh panthic support, is important for social harmony in Punjab, and blunts any appeal that Waris Punjab De might have. Repeated surveys also show that an alliance between the two parties would energise cadres,” a senior BJP leader said.
Waris Punjab De is a political outfit founded in 2021 around issues of the political rights of Sikhs, headed by incarcerated Lok Sabha MP Amritpal Singh.

articles.title: Karnataka moves Supreme Court to restrain Tamil Nadu in Cauvery–South Vellar–Vaigai–Gundar Link Project
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Karnataka argued that Tamil Nadu cannot undertake any work on the CVG Link without clearance from the Union government

The State of Karnataka has moved the Supreme Court seeking a temporary injunction against Tamil Nadu and the Union government with regard to the Cauvery (Kattalai)–South Vellar–Vaigai–Gundar Link Project (CVG Link) and related works for utilising surplus Cauvery waters flowing down from Karnataka.

The application for injunction has been filed in Karnataka’s original suit challenging the legality of the CVG Link, for which Tamil Nadu has sought the Union government’s ‘in-principle approval’, and declaration as a national project on January 5, 2021.

The court had disposed of a similar application in January last year, saying the Centre had not given in-principle approval to the CVG Link, and hence, it was not necessary to consider any interim relief at that point.

The new application filed a few days ago on November 20 submitted that Karnataka happened to come across an order passed by the Madras High Court which extracts a status report of Tamil Nadu stating that work on parts of the first phase of the CVG Link had been “going on since January 21, 2021”.

Karnataka alleged that these facts were not placed before the Supreme Court by Tamil Nadu. Karnataka said that, according to its information, several Phase-I structures have already been completed and land has been acquired for further works.
The State argued that Tamil Nadu cannot undertake any work on the CVG Link without clearance from the Union government. The works, if any, already undertaken by Tamil Nadu were illegal.
Farmers of southern districts disappointed with poor fund allocation for Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar river-linking project

In its application, Karnataka argued that Tamil Nadu has worked out the water for the project from the surpluses at Mettur Dam, placed at about 8.60 TMC at 50% dependability. Karnataka said the unilateral utilisation of surplus waters coming from Karnataka may later be relied upon by Tamil Nadu to claim equities, to the prejudice of Karnataka’s rights in the surplus waters of the Cauvery.

In its application, Karnataka has urged the court to restrain Tamil Nadu from executing the Cauvery–South Vellar Link Project (the first phase of the CVG Link), including the ongoing works, and from taking up any further works under Phase-I, Phase-II and Phase-III.

It has also sought a judicial direction to stop Tamil Nadu from executing or utilising non-Tamil Nadu Cauvery waters under other projects, including diversion of flood waters from Mettur Reservoir to the Sarabanga sub-basin, the New Kattalai Barrage at Mayanur, and barrages and check dams across the Cauvery and Kollidam.

Karnataka has asked the court to intervene and direct the Union government not to process Tamil Nadu’s January 2021 request for in-principle approval, and to refrain from declaring the CVG Link a national project.
Further, the State pressed the court to direct Tamil Nadu to demolish the works already completed in Phase I of the CVG Link.

articles.title: BJP MLA Rekha Patra’s condition improves, legislator remains under observation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rekha Patra is now able to speak and communicate any physical discomfort to doctors, while the slurring in her speech has also reduced significantly

The health condition of BJP MLA Rekha Patra has improved, with her slurred speech reducing considerably, but doctors have kept her in the intensive care unit (ICU) for close observation, hospital sources said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

The Hingalganj MLA was taken off ventilator support on Monday (November 23, 2026) and has not required it since. She is now able to speak and communicate any physical discomfort to doctors, while the slurring in her speech has also reduced significantly, BJP leader Archana Das Majumdar said.
However, the three-member medical team treating her is not willing to take any chances and has recommended that she remain in the ICU for continued monitoring.
Hospital sources said she was still receiving supplemental oxygen due to low oxygen levels in her body.
While other clinical parameters indicate a positive recovery, doctors remain concerned about possible complications arising from the poisoning.

Following the suspected poisoning, excessive saliva had accumulated in Ms. Patra's mouth. As she was not fully conscious, some saliva entered her lungs, affecting oxygen supply to the body, an earlier CT scan had found.
Doctors said the effects of impaired oxygen supply to the lungs may not become immediately apparent and could manifest after some delay.

A repeat CT scan of her chest was scheduled for Tuesday (November 24, 2026) afternoon to assess the extent of any lung damage. Her further recovery would depend, among other factors, on the findings of the scan, they said.
Meanwhile, doctors are yet to establish the exact composition of the suspected poison detected in her stomach.
According to the medical team, the substance found in her stomach was described as a herbal larvicide (herbal pesticide), but its precise ingredients remain unknown.
The container of the pesticide, details of which were provided by her family members, did not carry any information about its composition.
In the absence of clarity over the ingredients, doctors at the private hospital are continuing treatment based on the symptoms associated with poisoning.

articles.title: Sri Lanka’s Opposition lawmakers accuse government of preventing parliamentary debate on Imran Khan’s release
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Cannot entertain motion that could impact bilateral ties, said the Sri Lanka government
Opposition lawmakers in Sri Lanka have accused the government of preventing a parliamentary debate on the release of jailed former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan.

Last week, the state-run Daily News reported that the Sri Lankan Parliament was scheduled to hold an adjournment debate on November 21, 2026, on a motion moved by Opposition MP Ajith P. Perera, from the main Opposition party Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB or United People’s Power), calling for Mr. Khan’s release on humanitarian grounds. The debate did not take place. Mr. Perera expressed disappointment and said it was “regrettable that the motion has been rejected even before being debated.”

Defending the government’s position, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the government did not wish to entertain matters that could create “diplomatic tensions” or affect ties with Sri Lanka’s bilateral partners. However, Mr. Hemachandra observed that Mr. Perera was free to express his personal views on the matter during the time allocated to him in Parliament.

articles.title: What do lemurs and opera singers share?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back. In conversation with one of the researchers, Dr Chiara De Gregorio from the University of Warwick

Have you seen opera performers sing? You might notice how their mouths move according to how high their pitch needs to be. Imagine finding out a primate in the rainforests of Madagascar has been doing the same, possibly even before opera began?

With a pointy snout, large eyes and usually a long tail, you might have encountered this primate in one of your favourite movies, Madagascar. Remember King Julien, who loved to sing and dance? He was a type of lemur! So were Maurice and Mort, the two characters always around him.

Endemic (naturally found only in) to the island of Madagascar, lemurs are primates with diverse activity patterns, and even though they share a resemblance with other primates, they evolved independently from monkeys, apes, etc. They are considered to be the world’s most endangered mammals by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). This is mostly due to habitat loss, hunting and even unstable conservation efforts due to political and financial instabilities.

While most lemurs might survive in captivity, there are specific species like the indri which can only survive in their natural habitat, making it extremely important for us to protect the forests and their home. Today, let’s talk about this very species — the indri or babakoto!
One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. These black-and-white-coated primates are known for their loud, often complex, and haunting territorial songs. They often sing as duets or group choruses and even use opera-like vocal techniques to reach higher pitches. This was, in fact, a quite recent discovery.

Researchers from the University of Warwick and the University of Turin found that the world’s only singing lemur opens its mouth wider on higher notes, just like a trained soprano. The new study, published in PLOS Computational Biology , shows the first direct evidence that wild indris coordinate their mouth opening with the frequency of their songs.
The research team analysed 83 video recordings of 19 wild indris, combining field audio with markerless motion-tracking technology. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

“The opera singers back in the day, before mics became a thing, used to tweak the shape of their mouth to sing louder and to reach farther to the audience sitting at the back. Imagine finding the same technique being used in the middle of a rainforest in Madagascar,” laughed Dr Chiara De Gregorio, corresponding author and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Warwick.

Human singers are trained to widen their mouths as pitch rises, aligning the resonant frequencies of the vocal tract with the harmonics of the voice and amplifying the sound. For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t.

“Every time the pitch of an indri’s song rose, we could see its mouth opening wider, frame by frame,” said Dr De Gregorio. “It’s the kind of fine-tuned coordination between voice and body that we usually associate with trained human singers, not with a lemur singing from the forest canopy.”

This method is called vocal tract tuning (formant or resonance tuning), and it is the deliberate adjustment of the vocal tract’s shape via the jaw, tongue, lips, larynx, and pharynx to align its resonant frequencies with the sound harmonics produced by the vocal folds.

articles.title: Teenager arrested in online fraud case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The boy reportedly acted as an intermediary in an alleged online financial fraud involving bank accounts rented from students at Changaramkulam and nearby areas

The police arrested a teenage boy who reportedly acted as an intermediary in an alleged online financial fraud involving bank accounts rented from students at Changaramkulam and nearby areas. Around a dozen cases were registered in connection with the alleged fraud.

The accused allegedly persuaded students, including his friends and relatives, to allow money to be transferred to their bank accounts. Amounts ranging from ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh were deposited into each account. The account holders were paid up to ₹10,000 to withdraw the money and hand it over.

Several students who took part in the transactions without knowing their connection to the alleged fraud are now facing charges in cybercrime cases. The cases could affect their higher education, overseas travel, and prospects of securing government jobs, the police said.

The alleged fraud money was traced to Rajasthan. Following this, a police team from Rajasthan visited Changaramkulam and questioned the suspects. The police at Changaramkulam also registered a first information report (FIR) in connection with the case.

articles.title: Karnataka developing dedicated app for ST welfare schemes, says Raghumurthy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Minister for Scheduled Tribes Welfare T. Raghumurthy said in Mysuru on Tuesday that the State government is developing a dedicated mobile application to provide Scheduled Tribe (ST) beneficiaries with real-time information on various welfare schemes and departmental services.

Speaking at a review meeting with district officials at the Mysuru Zilla Panchayat hall, the Minister said the proposed app would bring information on all welfare schemes and facilities under a single digital platform, enabling beneficiaries to access details easily.

The government was also focusing on ensuring that welfare programmes reach all tribal communities, including more than 50 sub-tribes such as Valmiki, Nayaka, Kadu Kuruba, Jenu Kuruba, Soliga and Hakki Pikki, he said.

Referring to his recent visits to tribal hamlets or haadis , Mr. Raghumurthy said several infrastructure gaps and difficulties had come to his notice. He directed officials to take steps to ensure residents received all eligible government facilities.

He instructed officials to conduct targeted surveys in the hamlets and organise special camps to help residents obtain Aadhaar cards and income certificates, which were essential for securing ration cards.

Reviewing the progress of the housing project being implemented through the Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited, the Minister said 100 houses had been sanctioned for tribal hamlets. While 15 houses had been completed, the remaining 85 were under construction.
He assured officials that funds were available and directed them to expedite construction and ensure early completion of the houses.

Anil Chikkamadu, H.D. Kote MLA; G.D. Harish Gowda, Hunsur MLA; M. Ramappa, Karnataka State Bhovi Development Corporation chairman; G. Lakshmikantha Reddy, Deputy Commissioner; S. Yukesh Kumar, Zilla Panchayat CEO; Mallikarjun Baladandi, Superintendent of Police; M.K. Savita, Mysuru City Corporation Commissioner; Ashok D.R., ST Welfare Department Director; and Ashok Dudagunti, Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki ST Development Corporation Managing Director were present.

articles.title: Mysuru division gears up for better SSLC, II PU results
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The School Education Department has set its sights on significantly improving SSLC and II PU examination results in the Mysuru division, with officials and resource teachers in four districts directed to work towards securing a place among the State’s top-performing divisions.

Additional Chief Secretary to the Department of School Education and Literacy Rashmi V. Mahesh, who chaired a high-level review meeting and resource teachers’ training workshop in Mysuru on Tuesday, directed officials to identify even the weakest students in classrooms and provide them with special attention to improve their academic performance.

The meeting, held at Vidya Vikas College of Engineering on Bannur Road, reviewed preparations for the 2026-27 SSLC and II PU annual examinations in Mysuru, Mandya, Kodagu and Chamarajanagar districts.

Officials presented details of school-wise preparations and the implementation of various initiatives, including ‘Mission 110 Days’, ‘Kalika Mitra’, ‘Kalika Khathri Parikshe’, ‘Nanna Oduva Samaya’, Mission 60+’ and a series of preparatory examinations.
Interacting with resource teachers, Ms. Mahesh stressed the need for regular writing practice and special remedial teaching classes for students lagging in their studies.

“Examination results are not merely statistics; they open the doors to higher education and shape the future of every child,” she said, urging teachers and officials to focus not just on pass percentages but also on improving the quality of education.

She asked principals and lecturers to motivate every science student to appear for the CET with confidence and make use of the 7.5% special reservation available to students from rural backgrounds who have studied in government schools and colleges for admission to professional courses.
She called upon the four districts to work in a “mission-mode” approach to secure top rankings at the State level.

School Education Commissioner Prabhulingaswamy Kavalikatti, Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board Chairman and Director of Pre-University Education Bharat, Board Director (Examinations) Anita Nazare, Divisional Secretary and ex-officio Joint Director Vivekananda, Deputy Directors of School Education, DIET principals and Block Education Officers of the four districts attended the meeting.
Separate training sessions were conducted for resource teachers in six subjects — Kannada, English, Hindi, Mathematics, Science and Social Science.

Principals of PU colleges were also given specific guidelines on the effective use of blueprints, question banks and model question papers, besides ensuring time-bound writing practice to improve II PU results.

articles.title: DGP inaugurates advanced command centre in Nellore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Integrated facility aims to improve crime detection, law and order monitoring and public grievance redressal

Director-General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta inaugurated a state-of-the-art District Integrated Command and Control Centre above the Umesh Chandra Conference Hall at the Police Ground in Nellore on Tuesday. He also inaugurated the new Chinna Bazaar Police Station and participated in the bhoomi puja for the construction of men’s and women’s police barracks, a Public Grievance Redressal System (PGRS) Conference Hall and a Road Safety Control Room.

The Command and Control Centre integrates district-wide CCTV cameras, drones, emergency services and police monitoring systems on a single platform. It can monitor live footage from 30 drone cameras simultaneously and is equipped with Artificial Intelligence (AI), Facial Recognition Technology, CCTV 360, the Trinetra App and the LHMS system to identify suspected criminals and suspicious activities.

Mr. Gupta inspected the advanced technological systems at the centre and enquired about their functioning and operational capabilities. He appreciated its role in crime detection, investigation, law and order monitoring, issuing real-time instructions and ensuring the prompt resolution of public grievances.

He lauded the initiative towards technology-driven policing and said steps would be taken to replicate the model in other districts. He said the modern police station would help provide efficient and prompt services to the public. The new building would also offer a better working environment for police personnel, strengthen operational efficiency and promote people-friendly policing.

Superintendent of Police Ajitha Vejendla thanked the DGP for his encouragement and support in establishing the centre with advanced technological facilities. She said the initiative aimed to make policing more transparent, accountable and accessible to the public through technology, effective monitoring and prompt response.

articles.title: Woman, 14-year-old daughter drown in farm pond in Chickballapur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sadiqa accidentally slipped and fell into the water. In an attempt to save her daughter, Salma jumped into the pond
A 37-year-old woman and her 14-year-old daughter drowned in a farm pond near Nimmakayalahalli village in Chintamani taluk of Chickballapur district on Monday (November 23).

The deceased have been identified as Salma and her daughter Sadiqa, residents of Banashankari in Bengaluru. Originally from Nimmakayalahalli, Salma was visiting her native village along with her daughter.

According to the police, the mother and daughter had gone near a pond on the outskirts of the village when Sadiqa accidentally slipped and fell into the water. In an attempt to save her daughter, Salma jumped into the pond. However, both drowned, reportedly unaware of the depth of the water.

Personnel from the Fire and Emergency Services rushed to the spot and retrieved the bodies. The Battarahalli police visited the spot, conducted an inspection and registered a case. Further investigation is under way.

articles.title: Expanded NCD survey in Andhra Pradesh to cover four additional health conditions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In addition to the existing five major conditions, obesity, fatty liver disease, chronic respiratory conditions and mental health disorders are now a part of the exercise conducted every financial year

The Department of Health, Medical and Family Welfare has announced that health screenings being conducted in the State under the Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) survey will be expanded to cover four additional health conditions — obesity, fatty liver disease, chronic respiratory conditions and mental health disorders.
Until now, screening has been conducted for people aged 18 and above for five major health conditions — hypertension, diabetes, oral cancer, breast cancer and cervical cancer.
The health screenings will be conducted every financial year, and the survey for the financial year 2026–27 is expected to begin soon.
“The programme is being expanded, considering changing lifestyles, rising obesity levels and growing risk of other chronic diseases,” a release from the department said on Tuesday.

Participating in a virtual review meeting on the upcoming NCD programme, Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav briefed officials on the proposed changes and the precautions to be taken. “The focus is on identifying these diseases at an early stage before the problem becomes a serious one,” he said.

Under the new survey, individuals who are overweight will be identified at an early stage, and their risk of developing other health complications will be assessed. They will also receive guidance on dietary habits, physical activity and weight management. People with obesity, hypertension, diabetes and thyroid disorders will also be assessed for their risk of developing fatty liver disease.

The survey will also identify those with chronic respiratory conditions at an early stage. Those with symptoms will be examined by medical officers at the Primary Health Centres (PHCs). Patients requiring further investigations will be referred to the regional and district hospitals, where spirometers will be made available to assess lung function.

To assess the mental health condition of an individual, a questionnaire will be prepared, which will include questions to identify symptoms of depression, anxiety, memory-related problems and psychotic disorders.

Individuals identified as being at risk will undergo preliminary telephonic assessments through Tele-MANAS. Those requiring further medical evaluation will be referred to the appropriate healthcare facilities through the District Mental Health Programme.

The Minister directed the officials to adopt a Facial Recognition System (FRS)-based identification mechanism during the upcoming survey, which means biometric details would be collected during the survey for verification.

An Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) ID would be generated for individuals, and their medical records linked to it. Details of screenings, disease diagnosis, treatment and follow-up consultations would be digitally recorded.

articles.title: Lula draws the line amid Trump interference in Brazil’s close and tough election
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Lula says ‘Brazil does not fit in anyone’s backyard’ even as the country’s top intelligence agency raises the risk of U.S. interference in the October 4 elections to a ‘critical level’. In recent months, the Trump administration has put enormous pressure on Brazil through tariffs and sanctions

In an unprecedented move last Wednesday (September 23, 2026), Brazilian President Lula da Silva’s campaign asked the country’s Federal Supreme Court (STF) to “investigate the possible U.S. interference in the country’s electoral process”. Lula’s Workers’ Party (PT) also filed a case with the Superior Election Tribunal (TSE) against the far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, seeking a probe into alleged U.S. support for his campaign.

The petitions came the same day as 14 countries belonging to the Shield of the Americas, a group of right-wing Latin American governments assembled by U.S. President Donald Trump, signed a pact designating 24 drug-trafficking groups as “shared threats”. Brazil’s two criminal organisations, First Capital Command (PCC) and Red Command (CV), were among the groups mentioned in the deal. Lula immediately hit back at the decision. “Brazil does not underestimate the challenge posed by organized crime, but it does not intend to outsource the responsibility of protecting its citizens,” the Brazilian leader said in his speech at the United Nations.

In his UN speech, Lula minced no words about how the U.S. threat is being perceived in Brazil. “In Latin America and the Caribbean, geographical proximity to the world’s greatest military power is inescapable… But Brazil does not fit in anyone’s backyard,” Lula declared to loud applause. The Brazilian did not meet Mr. Trump in New York; instead, he engaged with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders, in what was seen as a political message to Mr. Trump.

Brazil goes to the polls on October 4 in a tense election. Lula leads Mr. Flávio by five points in the first-round polls. If they meet again in the second round on October 25, polls show a close race, adding to fears of U.S. interference influencing the result. In recent months, the Trump administration has put enormous pressure on Brazil through tariffs , sanctions and by classifying PCC and CV as terrorist organisations.

Adding to the concerns is a confidential report sent recently by Brazil’s Intelligence Agency (Abin) to the President and TSE. The report raised the risk of U.S. interference to a “critical level”. The Abin assessment, reported widely by the Brazilian media, says the “reaffirmation of U.S. hegemony” in Latin America is a priority for Washington, particularly to counter China’s influence over strategic assets.

Lula says ‘Brazil does not fit in anyone’s backyard’ even as the country’s top intelligence agency raises the risk of U.S. interference in the October 4 elections to a ‘critical level’. In recent months, the Trump administration has put enormous pressure on Brazil through tariffs and sanctions

In an unprecedented move last Wednesday (September 23, 2026), Brazilian President Lula da Silva’s campaign asked the country’s Federal Supreme Court (STF) to “investigate the possible U.S. interference in the country’s electoral process”. Lula’s Workers’ Party (PT) also filed a case with the Superior Election Tribunal (TSE) against the far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, seeking a probe into alleged U.S. support for his campaign.

The petitions came the same day as 14 countries belonging to the Shield of the Americas, a group of right-wing Latin American governments assembled by U.S. President Donald Trump, signed a pact designating 24 drug-trafficking groups as “shared threats”. Brazil’s two criminal organisations, First Capital Command (PCC) and Red Command (CV), were among the groups mentioned in the deal. Lula immediately hit back at the decision. “Brazil does not underestimate the challenge posed by organized crime, but it does not intend to outsource the responsibility of protecting its citizens,” the Brazilian leader said in his speech at the United Nations.

In his UN speech, Lula minced no words about how the U.S. threat is being perceived in Brazil. “In Latin America and the Caribbean, geographical proximity to the world’s greatest military power is inescapable… But Brazil does not fit in anyone’s backyard,” Lula declared to loud applause. The Brazilian did not meet Mr. Trump in New York; instead, he engaged with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders, in what was seen as a political message to Mr. Trump.

Brazil goes to the polls on October 4 in a tense election. Lula leads Mr. Flávio by five points in the first-round polls. If they meet again in the second round on October 25, polls show a close race, adding to fears of U.S. interference influencing the result. In recent months, the Trump administration has put enormous pressure on Brazil through tariffs , sanctions and by classifying PCC and CV as terrorist organisations.

articles.title: China announces shock corruption probe into Politburo member
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Shanghai Party Secretary Chen Jining was earlier expected to assume a top leadership role in 2027

A prominent Chinese politician who is a member of the ruling Communist Party of China’s Politburo and was widely tipped for a top national leadership position in 2027 was placed under a shock disciplinary investigation on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

The surprising announcement of “suspected severe violations” by Chen Jining, who has since 2022 been the top CPC leader in Shanghai and has served on the 25-member Politburo, left political observers in Beijing stunned.

Mr. Chen (62) was tipped to take on a prominent national role in the once-in-five-year Party Congress set for next year, which will see a major reshuffle. President Xi Jinping is expected to begin a fourth term in 2027.

Mr. Chen “is being investigated by the CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the National Commission of Supervision for suspected severe violations of discipline and laws,” a brief statement said.

Mr. Chen was previously the president of Mr. Xi’s alma mater, Tsinghua University, and served as the mayor of Beijing between 2018 and 2022, before his promotion to the Politburo as the Party Secretary of China’s financial centre, Shanghai.

In Shanghai, Mr. Chen was popular with foreign business representatives and is among the few leaders in the top echelons of the CPC with significant international exposure, having conducted his doctoral studies in environmental engineering at Imperial College London.

Politburo members are rarely investigated, and only half a dozen Politburo-level members in the last three decades have been removed. Notably, removals have often coincided with the run-up to Party Congresses that see leadership promotions and reshuffles.

Another former Shanghai Party Secretary, Chen Liangyu, was removed in 2006, a year before the 2007 Congress that saw the anointment of Mr. Xi as former leader Hu Jintao’s successor. The year of Mr. Xi’s ascension in 2012 saw the removal of Bo Xilai, then Party Secretary in Chongqing.

Under Mr. Xi, two Politburo-ranked members have been removed, including the former security chief Zhou Yongkang who retired from the Politburo Standing Committee, the party’s highest body, in 2012 and was placed under investigation in 2014. Another former Chongqing Party Secretary, Sun Zhengcai, was removed in 2017. Mr. Chen will likely be the third.

Mr. Chen was present at the CPC’s Fifth Plenum in Beijing last month, a key annual meeting that confirmed the expulsion of as many as 33 members of the party’s Central Committee, including 16 PLA Generals, and concluded with a pledge to “persevere with full and rigorous party self-governance”.

articles.title: Maharashtra panel recommends ₹10 crore fine, life imprisonment for those guilty of exam paper leaks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Panel, headed by TISS director, calls for task force and special courts to deal with leak cases, the creation of a body to manage exam venues, third-party audits, cyber security measures, and monitoring devices

People involved in leaking recruitment examination papers should be punished with a fine of ₹10 crore and life imprisonment, according to the recommendations of a committee set up by the Maharashtra government, which submitted its report on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

The panel, headed by the director of the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, also proposed a framework to oversee the process of conducting tests, including a third party audit and a new body to manage exam venues.

This committee was set up in the wake of a paper leak in an examination to recruit pharmacists and drug inspectors for 954 posts, conducted by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission on March 22. It was later discovered that the paper had already been leaked on WhatsApp, leading to the cancellation of the recruitment process on August 25, and an investigation into the matter. The State government set up the committee on September 4, after candidates sought a review of the exam process to recommend changes in the system.

Apart from a recommended penalty of a ₹10 crore fine and life imprisonment for individuals involved in paper leaks, the panel called for the establishment of a task force to address leak incidents, courts for the disposal of cases, and a body to manage exam venues, to bring accountability to district officials and prevent such leaks.

The panel proposes a third party audit, a cyber security cell, surveillance cameras, and signal-blocking devices at venues. Police personnel should be appointed to the Commission’s teams and non-governmental institutions need to be monitored to reduce irregularities in the selection of venues, the committee said. It also called for the publication of statistics regarding vacant posts and the development of a portal to resolve issues faced by candidates.

With regard to the pharmacist selection exam, the report recommends a fee refund by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission for all candidates who file income tax returns. The panel also suggested an increase in the number of posts for the Group-C exam, an extra attempt for candidates, an exam schedule to be announced by October, and a grievance portal to ensure transparency.

articles.title: KSEB revokes suspension of engineer over power disruption during Minister’s programme in Kannur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) has revoked the suspension of Satheesh Babu P.V., a sub-engineer attached to the Kannur electrical section. He was suspended following a power disruption during a programme attended by Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph at the Jawahar Library Hall in Kannur on November 21.

The suspension was withdrawn through an order issued by the executive engineer on Tuesday (November 24), following a review of the circumstances surrounding the incident and the report submitted by senior officials. Mr. Babu had been suspended pending inquiry after power supply was disrupted during the Minister’s programme on the morning of November 21.
The decision to reconsider the suspension followed a direction from the Deputy Chief Engineer, Electrical Circle, Kannur, on November 23.
In his report, the assistant executive engineer said that the official was unaware of the programme attended by the Minister and had intended to carry out routine maintenance work.
The suspension had triggered protests from KSEB employees’ organisations.
